toc.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence

  • What the exam is: 60 items, 120 minutes, a scaled score of 720 to pass
  • The seven domains, their weights and the 30 objectives behind them
  • The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for
  • The decision rules that explain most correct answers
  • How the course is built and how to use it

Who this exam is for. A professional who uses Claude every day as a productivity tool in operations, marketing, project management, education or communications, and who builds Claude Projects for their team. No coding is needed. It is not for developers who build against the API or design agents; those people escalate to Claude Developers and Architects.

2The Exam at a Glance

Fact Value (guide v1.0, July 2026)
Credential / code Claude Associate – Foundations / CCAO-F
Items 60, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select
Time 120 minutes (2 minutes per item)
Passing score 720 on a scaled range of 100 to 1,000 (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking)
Fee USD 99 per attempt [Verify live]
Delivery Proctored by Pearson VUE: online or at a test center
Validity 12 months from the date the credential is awarded; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment
Retakes Wait 14 days after the first failed attempt, 30 after the second, 90 after the third; at most 4 attempts in a rolling 12 months; limits are per exam
Prerequisites None are required; regular hands-on use of Claude is recommended; no software or API experience is needed
Score report Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail)
Exam tip

For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

3The Seven Domains

Domain Weight What it asks you to do Modules
D2 Output Evaluation and Validation 21% Check accuracy and completeness; spot hallucinations, inconsistencies and bias; fact-check; know when a human must review; edit and adapt; choose output formats 3 to 5
D4 Workflow Integration and Solution Design 16% Analyze requirements; research and plan; support design; fit Claude into workflows; explain value and limits 9, 10
D6 Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use 15% Appropriate and inappropriate uses; data sensitivity and privacy; organizational policy; ethics 13, 14
D1 Prompting and Task Execution 14% Write effective prompts; decompose tasks; iterate; adapt to the task type 1, 2
D3 Product and Model Selection 12% Choose features; tell Haiku, Sonnet and Opus apart; manage context and memory 6 to 8
D5 Configuration and Knowledge Management 12% Configure Projects; manage knowledge and connectors; write system-level instructions; keep them current 11, 12
D7 Troubleshooting and Optimization 10% Diagnose weak prompts and poor outputs; adjust on feedback; optimize workflows 15, 16
  • Of 60 items, about 13 come from D2, 10 from D4, 9 from D6, 8 from D1, 7 each from D3 and D5, and 6 from D7.
  • Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Items are written against the 30 objectives listed in the guide.
  • Study order by value: D2 first, then D4, D6 and D1. Every domain is at least 10%, so none can be skipped.
Exam tip

No domain is small. The weakest domain on your practice results is the cheapest place to gain points.

4The Minimally Qualified Candidate

Running case

Cedarbrook Outfitters

  • Throughout the course you follow Cedarbrook Outfitters, a fictional outdoor-gear retailer
  • Its operations, marketing and customer-care teams adopt Claude for reports, campaign copy, reply drafts and planning
  • Each module solves one problem the teams meet; the questions use the same style as the exam

The minimally qualified candidate (MQC) can:

  • turn a business goal into a clear, structured prompt, and break big requests into steps
  • check Claude's output for accuracy, completeness and bias before anyone relies on it
  • choose the right feature (chat, search, Research, Projects, Artifacts) and the right model for the job
  • configure a Project with instructions and knowledge, and connect tools such as Google Drive
  • protect sensitive data and follow the organization's AI policy
  • fix weak outputs and tune workflows
  • recognize limits and escalate technical work to Developers and Architects

5Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward

Most items describe a business situation and ask for the best action. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

# Rule Typical wrong answers
1 Verify facts, numbers and citations against an authoritative source before sharing "Claude sounded confident", "ask Claude to rate itself"
2 Be specific: goal, audience, context, format and constraints in the prompt A vague one-line request, or "just retry"
3 Break complex work into steps and review each One giant prompt with no review
4 Match the model and effort to the task: lighter for routine and high-volume, stronger for hard reasoning "Always the biggest model", "never use Research"
5 Use the lightest feature that fits: chat for quick, web search for current facts, Research for deep reports Research for a one-line fact
6 Put standing context in a Project (instructions and knowledge), not in every prompt Pasting the same background each time
7 Protect sensitive data: remove or anonymize identifiers; follow policy; use approved tools "Tell Claude not to retain it", uploading as-is
8 Keep a qualified human in the loop for high-stakes or regulated decisions Letting Claude decide alone
9 Start a fresh chat or summarize when a conversation gets long or drifts Piling on more messages
10 Escalate technical, integration or architecture work to Developers or Architects Improvising an API integration
Exam tip

When two options both work, prefer the one that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable.

6How to Use This Course

  • Order: read modules 1 to 16 in order (they follow the domains), then module 17 (recap) and 18 (technique).
  • Each module has the objectives it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card.
  • Practice on the real product. The guide recommends building a Project with instructions and knowledge and evaluating outputs for accuracy and bias. Do the small exercises as you read.
  • Product details change fast. Boxes marked [Verify live] show current behavior (plan limits, menu names, model lineup). On the exam, answer by the principle and check the Help Center for current details.
  • Independence. This course is independent study material; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic or Pearson VUE. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

7Exam Q&A

S1A marketing coordinator has used Claude daily for a year and has never written code. Does the exam guide set a prerequisite they fail?

  • AYes: at least one year of API experience is required before anyone can register for the exam
  • BNo: there are no mandatory prerequisites and no software or API experience is needed
  • CYes: a software-development or data-science background of several years is required for all candidates
  • DYes: an earlier Anthropic course must be completed first
Show the answer

Answer: B. The guide recommends hands-on experience with Claude but requires nothing, and no API experience is needed.

S2Which domain carries the largest share of the scored items?

  • AOutput Evaluation and Validation
  • BPrompting and Task Execution
  • CTroubleshooting and Optimization
  • DProduct and Model Selection
Show the answer

Answer: A. Output Evaluation and Validation is 21%, more than any other domain.

S3A candidate scored 700 overall but 95 percent in one domain. What is the result?

  • APass, because domains average out
  • BPass, because one domain is high
  • CFail, because the total scaled score is below 720
  • DFail, because every domain must reach 720
Show the answer

Answer: C. The pass decision uses the total scaled score; domain percentages are reported for guidance only.

S4Which person is the exam written for?

  • AA professional who uses Claude as a productivity tool and builds Projects for their team
  • BA software engineer who builds agents and applications directly against the Claude API every day
  • CAn executive who has never used Claude but approves the budget for AI tools in the company
  • DA machine-learning specialist who trains models
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Associate credential targets everyday productivity users; builders of APIs and agents sit in the Developer and Architect credentials.
